plan.english: The serpent was great and heavy. He shut the waters in the mountain, and the waters were not going forth. The rye dried up, and the cattle were thirsty. Then the god of thunder came to it. He slew the serpent with a stone. He split it, and the waters ran forth. He freed the cattle from it. The cattle were free. The thunder sounded, and the cloud rained. Then they gave him great fame. Then he rode away on horses. The rye grew.

God of thunder, you who struck the serpent with a stone, you who released the waters from the height, you who freed the cattle, you who drive swift horses! At your feet the sea trembles. You give us heavy rain. Do not make our fields dry! Your imperishable fame lives. Now, giver of rain, hear us! Give us cattle and good fame.

The sister said to the brother: "Who struck the serpent?" Then the brother said to her: "The giver of rain struck the serpent." She said: "With what did he strike it?" "With a stone and with thunder," said the brother. "Having struck it, he released the waters." Then she said: "Did the serpent die?" "It died, and the waters ran to the sea." Then she said: "His name is famous."

The serpent shut the cattle in the mountain. The cattle made a noise in the darkness. Then the giver of rain sought them. He heard them. He saw the serpent on the height. He said to it: "Serpent, release the cattle! If you do not release them, I shall strike you with this stone." But it did not release them. Then he struck it on the head with a rock, and it died. The cattle came out of the mountain. He led the cattle to the field. Then his heart rejoiced.

A serpent lay in the deep sea. It swallowed the water of the rivers. The rivers did not arrive at the sea. The berries dried up. Then the giver of rain came to the sea. The serpent saw him, and trembled. He struck the serpent on the neck. The serpent let go of it. They ran to the sea. The berries became full. Then he went away.

Cloud, come! Cloud, rain on the fields! May the waters go forth from the height. May the berries be full. May the cattle not be thirsty, and may they not grow tired. May the cattle and the horses live. May the serpent die who shut in the waters. May the stream be full. May the sheep drink them. Cloud, give us water!

A heavy stone stood in the deep stream, and the stream did not go forth. The cattle lay by the stream, and were thirsty. Then the giver of rain came to the stream. He pushed it with his foot. It split, and it went forth. The stream goes to the river; the river goes to the sea. His imperishable fame lives.

title: Prayer to the God of the Rain-Cloud

plan.english: God of the rain-cloud, come to us! You are great. Bring rain to us! Slay the serpent who shut in the waters! Do not leave us! Hear our word! Protect our sheep! May the wolf not eat them. May our cattle live, and may our rye be thriving. Then we shall give you mead.

title: The Two Brothers and the Serpent

plan.english: The serpent struck the god, and he lay down. Then the god's brother came. He said to him: "Brother, stand up, and strike the serpent!" He stood up, and grew strong. The two of them struck the serpent, and it died. Then he released the waters. Great was their fame.

Waters, you who went forth from the height, you who go to the sea! You nourish the fields. You fill the rivers. You are the mothers of the rivers. Your fame is imperishable. Come to us! Waters, listen to me! Protect our cattle!

The rye dried up, and the cattle were thirsty, and they sweated. Then the men looked at the sky. They said: "Where is the rain-cloud?" Then the cloud came from the height. The cloud rained. The streams filled, and the rye grew. The apples were thriving. Then they rejoiced.

The god of thunder drove swift horses. Thunder went, and the rain-cloud followed him. His wheels turned. Then the serpent saw him, and trembled, and crept down. He slew the serpent. He released the waters. Then he went away.

Sky lay on Earth, and he was heavy, and darkness was there. Then a great god split Sky and Earth apart. He lifted it up, and made it stand above. He laid the earth below. Then light came forth, and the darkness went away. The earth was broad, and the sky was great.

A man and his own twin dwelt there. Then the man slew his own twin. From the flesh of the twin the gods made the earth. From his head they made the sky. From his foot they built the mountains. From his ear they created the waters. From his heart they made fire. Then he looked up, and he trembled in fear. The sky stood above, and she lay below.

title: Hymn to Father Sky and Mother Earth

plan.english: Father Sky, hear us! You who give rain, you who give light to us! Mother Earth, listen to us! You who nourish the cattle, you who carry the mountains! Give us good fame. Mother, give us rye and wool.

Who stretched out the heavy sky above? Who laid the earth below? Who let the waters go to the deep sea? Who made swift light above? The great god stretched out the sky, and laid her below, and let them go to the sea, and made light. To which god shall we give mead? To him we shall give mead.

The gods put sky and earth in order. The sun climbs by its own path. Dawn comes, and it follows her. The waters go to the deep sea, and the cattle go to the field. The cloud rains, and the waters fill the rivers, and the apples ripen. Let us go by this path.
The son said to his father: "Who holds up the sky?" The father said to him: "The gods hold it up. Look up, son!" Then the son said: "And who protects the gods?" "Father Sky protects them."

Dawn, daughter of Sky, shine for us! You who drive away the darkness, you who awaken us again, you who lead the cattle to the field, you who are red above again! Your light is good. Dawn, give us light.

title: The Counsel of the Old Man

plan.english: The old father-in-law said to his own son-in-law: "Son-in-law, hear my word. Son-in-law, listen well! Whoever does not know the path goes astray. Do not tremble, son-in-law. Give mead to the gods, and your cattle will live. Go by this path."

Mother, we plough your field. Be good to us, and may the rye grow, and the seed and the apples. May the wolf not come to us. May the dog protect the sheep. May the rain-cloud rain on the rye. We shall give you mead, Mother.

title: The Wedding of the Sun's Daughter

plan.english: The Sun's daughter shone. Then the two sons of Sky arrived on horses. The Sun said to her: "They have grown fond of you." She said: "I shall go with them." Then he gave her to them. She dressed herself in a good garment, and wore silver. The two placed her on the chariot of silver, and led her away. The gods drank mead, and they rejoiced. Then Dawn shone. She was red. The wheel of the sun went forth.

A twin arrived at the Sun. He said: "Sun, give me your daughter! I shall give you ten cattle and four horses." The father said: "Be my son-in-law." Then the twin gave them, and the father gave him his own daughter. Then the two of them drank.

The Sun's daughter sank in the deep sea. The mother sought her own daughter. She said to Dawn: "Dawn, did you see her?" Dawn said to her: "I saw her. She sank there." Then the mother said to the twins: "Twins, rescue her from the sea!" The twins heard her. Carried by horses, they came to the sea. They seized the daughter, and drew her out of the sea. She was rescued. The mother rejoiced, and gave good fame to the twins.
Sun, you who look upon the sea, you who drive swift horses! The deep darkness goes away. You ripen the berries and the apples. Hear us! Do not leave us! Heat us!

Swift twins, come to us! You who rescued us from the sea, you who drive swift horses, you who draw the wheel, you who tame the horses! Twins, hear us! Protect our horses. May our horses be healthy. Givers of good things, give us horses!

title: The Twins Save a Man from the Sea

plan.english: A man swam in the sea, and grew tired. The cloud rained, and the sea boiled. Then he trembled in fear, and sank. He said: "Twins, rescue me from the sea!" The twins heard him. The two horses ran through the waters. The twins, having taken him, lifted him, and led him out. He lay down. Then he gave a horse to the twins.

There were two twins. One of the two died, and one of the two lived. He grew tired. Then he went to the sky. "Father Sky, give me my brother!" he said. Sky said to him: "Your brother shall live in the sky. You shall live below. You shall go to him, and he shall come to you."

title: The Birth of the Thunder God

plan.english: The god of thunder is born! Great is his stature. At his birth the mountain trembles. The sea boils. Sky is his father. Swift horses carry him. He will strike the serpent, and he will let the waters go. May he give us rain!

Dawn came forth out of the darkness. She was red. She was the daughter of Sky. Then Sky saw her, and he rejoiced. Her light went forth. The goose woke up, and she awakened the cattle. The darkness vanished. Then he set a famous name on her.

Agni, you who are born in the waters, you who are red, you who dwell with us! You heat the water, and cook the meat. In the darkness your light shines. Agni, sit down with us! Agni, drink the poured mead!

title: The Goddess, the Wolf and the Sheep

plan.english: A goddess dwelt at the spring. The sheep came to the spring, and drank the water. Then the one-eyed wolf crept toward the sheep. He seized a sheep. The dog saw the wolf. Then the goddess said to the dog: "Dog, seize the wolf!" Then the dog seized the wolf, and the wolf let the sheep go. The goddess smeared them with grease. Then the goddess gave good wool to the sheep.

A sister saw a god on the height, and was afraid. She said to her own brother: "Who is he?" The brother said to her: "He is the giver of rain, and he strikes the serpent." Then she spoke: "Let us give him a stallion." Then the two of them gave him a stallion.

Gods and goddesses, hear us! You who dwell in the sky, you who sit on the heights, you who go through the deep waters! We give you the poured mead. Protect us! May our cattle be healthy. Give us swift horses!

Fire was with the gods. It was not with men. Then a man went to the mountain of the gods. Having seized the fire, he hid it in a heavy stone. Then he went down, and sweated. Sky saw him, and said to him: "Give the fire back!" Then he answered: "I shall not give it back." Then he struck it with thunder, and it split. And it went back to them. Now they seek it in the stone.

Agni ran away from the gods, and went down into the waters. The gods sought him. They did not find him. A goose was swimming. Then it saw him there, and said to them: "Agni is in the water." They said: "Agni, come forth from the water!" Agni said: "I am afraid." Then Agni came forth from it.

The sea swelled, and the fire vanished. Then the men became cold, and trembled. They said: "Who will bring us fire?" Then the dog said: "I shall bring it to you." The dog arrived at the height of the gods. Having seized the fire, the dog ran back. Then he carried it to them. They brought him meat. He ate it. Now he dwells with them.
Stone, give us fire! It is inside. Come out of it! Burn up! Heat us!

A sister, being thirsty, arrived at the deep spring. She said to the goddess of the spring: "Goddess of the spring, give me water!" The goddess said to her: "Drink the water! The water is healthy. Do not urinate in the spring. Whoever urinates in the spring, let him be thirsty." She drank the water, and went away.
If a man urinates in the river, let the goddess strike him. Whoever urinates in the stream, let the waters hit him. Whoever puts filth into the spring, let him go away from the field.
